flawed_step: 0034 (Step 7): The proof does not justify that a neighbor of v_k in V_{k-1} has a neighbor in V_{k-2}, nor that the required chain continues through every color class.
assessment_summary:
0001: Merely labels the solution; no mathematical claim.
0002: States the theorem to be proved.
0003: Correctly completes the theorem statement.
0004: Introduces the proof structure; no inference.
0005: The lemma is valid for finite graphs under the standard meaning of k-critical.
0006: If G is not vertex-critical, such a removable vertex exists by definition.
0007: Repeated removal preserves chromatic number k.
0008: For a finite graph the process terminates at a k-critical subgraph.
0009: States the standard minimum-degree lemma for critical graphs.
0010: Merely completes the notation in the lemma statement.
0011: Correctly begins a contradiction argument from d(v)<k-1.
0012: Criticality gives a (k-1)-coloring of H-v, and at most k-2 neighbor colors leave an available color for v.
0013: Correctly obtains a contradiction to chi(H)=k.
0014: Transition to the main proof; no inference.
0015: Correctly applies Lemma 2 to G.
0016: Correctly completes the selection of H.
0017: Correctly applies the minimum-degree lemma; indeed every vertex of H has degree at least k-1.
0018: Correctly completes the choice of v_k.
0019: By k-criticality, H-v_k is (k-1)-colorable.
0020: Correctly denotes the color classes of such a proper coloring.
0021: Adding the singleton {v_k} produces a partition of V(H) into k independent sets.
0022: Correctly introduces an orientation rule for H.
0023: Orienting every cross-class edge toward the higher-indexed class is well-defined.
0024: There are actually no within-class edges, so this clause is vacuous and harmless.
0025: The claimed acyclicity is correct, subject to the following explanation.
0026: Along every cross-class directed edge the class index strictly increases, so a directed cycle cannot traverse distinct classes.
0027: Correctly notes that a return from a higher to a lower class is impossible, though the wording about requiring both directions is imprecise.
0028: Correctly observes that no cycle can lie within a color class.
0029: Correctly justifies independence of V_1,...,V_{k-1} and the triviality of V_k.
0030: Introduces the analysis of longest directed paths; no inference.
0031: Correct: every directed edge strictly increases the class index, since there are no within-class edges.
0032: Correctly begins the resulting upper bound.
0033: Correct: every directed path in H contains at most one vertex from each of the k classes.
0034: Not justified: v_k has a neighbor in each color class, but a chosen neighbor in V_{k-1} need not have a neighbor in V_{k-2}; the asserted chain is not established.
0035: The proposed continuation through successively lower classes remains unsupported.
0036: If such a chain existed its orientation would lead from V_1 to v_k, but its existence has not been proved.
0037: Page marker only; no mathematical claim.
0038: Blank line; no mathematical claim.
0039: Labels Step 8; no inference.
0040: An arbitrary orientation does extend the partial orientation to all edges of G, but it gives no path-length control.
0041: Incorrect: vertices and edges outside H can create directed paths longer than k under an arbitrary extension.
0042: The fact that H has no longer path says nothing about paths using vertices outside H.
0043: The conclusion is unsupported because neither the required k-vertex path in H nor the global upper bound in G was proved.
0044: Merely completes the unsupported conclusion.
